findings.where: script[11]-[12] and outcomes waterfront_spindrift lines[2], waterfront_mooring_post lines[0]-[1]
findings.issue: Maya restates her budget with the same device as level_17. Level_17: 'a three-sign place and i'll still come, but i'll sigh at the bill so loudly the gulls fly off', paid off at Pelican Steps with 'exactly as promised'. Level_18: 'a three-sign place won't ruin me. but i will read the bill out loud', paid off at Mooring Post with 'as promised'. The clue still reads as one star, but it is a bill-theatrics threat plus 'as promised' payoff in back-to-back levels, and levels 19 and 20 must restate the budget again.
findings.suggested_fix: script[11] maya: 'three signs won't sink me anymore. but i will bring it up at every dinner from now until i'm on that coast' (ANNOYED, clue budget). script[12] brooke: 'a whole summer of hearing about one bill. honestly, tempting' (HAPPY, clue null). Outcomes: waterfront_spindrift lines[2] maya: 'two dollar signs. nothing to bring up at future dinners. you're all very lucky' (HAPPY). waterfront_mooring_post lines[0] maya: 'three dollar signs. it was delicious, and i will be mentioning it at every dinner until the coast. starting now' (ANNOYED); lines[1] brooke: 'worth it. dessert's on me, so at least that part stays off the list' (HAPPY).

findings.where: script[15]-[16] (Brooke: 'i just drove six hours back from my sister's, fuelled entirely by gas-station snacks' / 'so tonight my dinner has to be the opposite of a gas station...') and outcomes waterfront_halyard lines[0]
findings.issue: Brooke's healthy wish is justified by a recent junk-food overload for the third level running (level_16 'a whole summer of night-market fryers', level_17 the housewarming's fried dough and whipped cream, now gas-station snacks), with the familiar setup-then-'so tonight' two-line shape. The writer brief bans reusing what justifies a vibe from the last 3 levels. Brooke is health-conscious by nature, so she needs no backstory, and her 'and in return' trade for conceding the quiet room already gives the line a reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete script[15]. Replace script[16] with brooke: 'and in return, my one ask for the food: simple and light. nothing that's been battered and dunked in hot oil' (NEUTRAL, clue vibe:healthy). The chat drops to 17 lines. waterfront_halyard lines[0] brooke: 'every roll here comes battered and fried. i gave up my noisy room tonight and still got the fryer' (ANNOYED).

findings.where: venue waterfront_spindrift review 2 and venue waterfront_mooring_post review 2
findings.issue: The chat sets the vegetarian standard as 'a whole part of the menu with no fish and no meat' / 'a whole page of rolls'. Starboard has 'one full page', Halyard 'the side of the menu', Ropewalk the green plates, but the answer's 'garden set' can read as a single set meal, so a careful player may briefly doubt it beside Starboard. Separately, Spindrift's 'The crunch on the rolls is toasted rice' and Mooring Post's 'The only crunch all night was toasted sesame' repeat one phrasing in the same level (also used in level_17's Sea Glass and Pelican Steps).
findings.suggested_fix: Spindrift review 2: replace 'Spindrift's garden set changed that:' with 'Spindrift gives fish- and meat-free pieces their own page of the menu, and it changed that:'. Mooring Post review 2: replace 'The only crunch all night was toasted sesame.' with 'Whatever was scattered on top, it was toasted sesame every time.'

summary: A warm, well-built level. Cyrus's eleven failed home rolls make a funny implied sushi craving that a careful player will find without the word ever appearing. Sushi day continuity is right: Cyrus and Mina were there in level_08, Brooke wasn't, and she heard it retold in level_10. Mina's request for a hushed room to hear Maya's news is in her voice, and Brooke's concession fits her. Every review evidences its deciding attribute: Ropewalk's bells, shouting chefs and loud playlist read as a clear one-star quiet miss, Mooring Post's 'clear step up in price' matches $$$, and Spindrift's peanut-allergy support group dinner is as firm as any decoy's evidence. The outcomes match the reviews (Starboard's peanut dressing on the vegetable page and crushed peanuts on the spinach, Gull Point's eel sauce and cured salmon, Halyard's fryer, Cormorant's quiet Greek), and Cormorant stays consistent with level_16, down to the napkin boats. Difficulty is about level with 16-17, not harder: peanut, quiet, budget and healthy are close to stated, and the challenge is telling five near-identical sushi counters apart from their reviews. The suggestions refresh devices repeated from level_17 (Maya's bill-theatrics restatement, Brooke's junk-food backstory, Maya's fail line, Ropewalk's triple-'not' quote), soften one over-explicit peanut line, and firm up Spindrift's vegetable-menu wording.
